frequency_question: How often do bilateral water-sharing treaties get successfully renewed by the original signatory governments prior to expiration when both states rely on the shared basin?
membership_rule: Includes formal transboundary river treaties between sovereign states that reached a scheduled expiration or renewal milestone. Excludes unilateral declarations, failed initial negotiations that never reached a treaty, and non-water security pacts.

cases.name: 1959 India-Pakistan Indus Waters Treaty continuous implementation
1995 Mekong Agreement replacement of 1957 Mekong Treaty
Soviet-Finnish Frontier Water Commission agreement renewals
Southern African Development Community (SADC) Revised Protocol on Shared Watercourses
Senegal River Basin Development Organization (OMVS) convention renewals

provenance_note: 6 cases named, 7 claimed via skeleton x multiplier
coverage_note: 6 named; believed roughly 7 in total for major basin treaties reaching direct renewal milestones in developing/developed interstate contexts.
known_gaps: Excludes minor bilateral sub-basin agreements with negligible public reporting.
skeleton: Regional water basin treaty renewals globally over 5 decades, categorized by sustained mutual utility.
multiplier: 6 hits out of 7 major structural renewals attempted where principals maintained baseline agricultural/political alignment.
validity_reason: International water diplomacy norms and structural hydrological dependencies change slowly over multi-year horizons.
